sources: synthetic smoke and direct module check output from 2026-09-21

findings.evidence: The user-requested raw neural output is clamped at the fitting-history floor before QLIKE. PyTorch gives zero gradient to raw outputs below that floor, so a run with every initial prediction below the floor can stall; the synthetic check confirms this derivative.
findings.fix: If actual fitting runs stall, revisit the requested raw-output constraint with the user and select an explicitly approved positive output parameterization or initialization.

findings.evidence: The synthetic smoke exercises train/predict for every module and invokes the full command line flow for HAR, but does not invoke the other eight command line entry points with synthetic data.
findings.fix: Run each remaining python -m models.<name> command on the synthetic database if entry point coverage is required beyond the tested module APIs.
